title: Explorer-Zero: Improving Self-Play for Long-Horizon Tasks with Decomposable Verifiable Rewards
abstract: arXiv:2610.19868v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Training LLM agents on long-horizon interactive tasks with reinforcement learning typically relies on human-annotated tasks and reliable verification, both expensive to construct for stateful environments. Self-play offers an alternative, but must generate achievable, compositional tasks and provide feedback beyond binary outcomes. We propose Explorer-Zero, a self-play framework that jointly generates tasks and fine-grained, verifiable rewards through environment interaction. A learned proposer explores the environment, constructs tasks, and records intermediate and final states as verification targets. These checkpoints reward partial completion, while alternating proposer--solver training adapts the generated curriculum. We show theoretically that subtask rewards reduce collapse among unsuccessful rollouts when they complete different numbers of subtasks. translated_title: Explorer-Zero：通过可分解的可验证奖励改进长程任务的自博弈
translated_abstract: 使用强化学习在长程交互任务上训练大语言模型（LLM）智能体，通常依赖于人工标注的任务和可靠的验证机制，而对于有状态的环境而言，这两者的构建成本都非常高。自博弈提供了一种替代方案，但它必须生成可实现的、可组合的任务，并提供超越二元结果的反馈。我们提出了 Explorer-Zero，一个通过与环境的交互来联合生成任务和细粒度、可验证奖励的自博弈框架。一个经过学习的提议者探索环境、构建任务，并将中间状态和最终状态记录为验证目标。这些检查点能够对部分完成给予奖励，同时通过提议者与求解者的交替训练来调整生成的课程。我们从理论上证明，当失败的回放轨迹完成了不同数量的子任务时，子任务奖励能够减少这些失败轨迹之间的坍缩。在无需人工标注训练任务的情况下，Explorer-Zero 的表现优于所评估的基线方法。
tldr: Explorer-Zero 提出了一种自博弈框架，通过与环境的交互同时自动生成任务和细粒度的可验证奖励，利用中间与最终状态检查点奖励部分完成，从而无需人工标注任务即可提升 LLM 智能体在长程任务上的强化学习效果。
en_tdlr: Explorer-Zero is a self-play framework that jointly generates tasks and fine-grained verifiable rewards through environment interaction, using intermediate and final state checkpoints to reward partial completion, enabling improved reinforcement learning of LLM agents on long-horizon tasks without human-annotated training data.
